_meta.indication: Brineura is indicated to slow the loss of ambulation in symptomatic pediatric patients 3 years of age and older with late infantile neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis type 2 (CLN2), also known as tripeptidyl peptidase 1 (TPP1) deficiency.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 190-201 (with open-label extension Study 190-202), compared to natural history control Study 190-901
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Single-arm, open-label dose-escalation study with extension; Brineura-treated patients compared to an independent untreated natural history cohort (Study 190-901).
pivotal_trials.population: Symptomatic pediatric patients aged 3 to 8 years with late-infantile CLN2 disease confirmed by TPP1 deficiency, with baseline combined Motor-Language score ≥ 3 (at least 1 in each domain).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Responder analysis: absence of an unreversed (sustained) 2-category decline or an unreversed score of 0 in the Motor domain of the CLN2 Clinical Rating Scale, over 96 weeks, versus the natural history cohort.
pivotal_trials.n: 24 patients enrolled in the Brineura single-arm study (22 evaluable for efficacy at week 96); compared to 42 untreated patients from the natural history cohort.
pivotal_trials.result: Adjusted logistic model: odds of not declining by 96 weeks were 13 times higher for Brineura-treated patients (Odds Ratio 13.1; 95% CI 1.2, 146.9). Unadjusted: 21 (95%) of 22 treated patients did not decline vs 21 (50%) of 42 natural history patients experiencing decline over 96 weeks.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥8%): pyrexia (71%), ECG abnormalities (71%), decreased CSF protein (71%), vomiting (63%), seizures (50%), hypersensitivity (46%), increased CSF protein (21%), hematoma (21%). Serious risks include intraventricular access device-related complications/infections and hypersensitivity reactions (11/24, 46%); cardiovascular reactions including hypotension (8%) and bradycardia (8%).
target_moa: Cerliponase alfa is recombinant human tripeptidyl peptidase-1 (TPP1), given as enzyme replacement therapy to restore TPP1 activity in the CNS; TPP1 deficiency causes accumulation of lysosomal storage material leading to progressive decline in motor function.
modality: Enzyme (recombinant human tripeptidyl peptidase-1 enzyme replacement therapy)

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee Meeting was held; review issues were addressed by the review teams.

description.text: Expanded the treatment population to birth (from the prior age restriction) for CLN2 disease

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application provides for an expansion of the treatment population to birth, corresponding updates to Indication and Usage, Dosing and Administration, and other sections of the Brineura Prescribing Information, as well as new information on infusion-associated reactions in the Warnings and Precautions section.

basis.text: Breakthrough Therapy Designation was granted for cerliponase alfa for the CLN2 indication on August 27, 2016 (after an initial denial).

citations.quote: A Breakthrough Therapy Designation request for cerliponase alfa was initially denied, and after submission of additional analyses/data, Breakthrough Therapy Designation was granted on August 27, 2016.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation granted April 1, 2013 (orphan designation 13-3919) for CLN2 disease.

citations.quote: The Brineura (cerliponase alfa) development program was granted orphan drug designation on April 1, 2013.

Brineura was granted orphan drug status (April 1, 2013, orphan designation 13-3919) and therefore is exempt from the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA) required assessment of the safety and effectiveness of the product for the claimed indication in pediatric patients.

basis.text: The BLA was granted Priority Review; Brineura also received a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher.

citations.quote: Brineura received a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher.

summary.text: Brineura was granted Orphan Drug Designation (April 1, 2013) and Breakthrough Therapy Designation (August 27, 2016), and the BLA received Priority Review plus a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher. It was a traditional (not accelerated) approval based on Study 190-201/202 compared with the DEM-CHILD natural history cohort; no Advisory Committee meeting was held.

citations.quote: The Brineura (cerliponase alfa) development program was granted orphan drug designation on April 1, 2013. A Breakthrough Therapy Designation request for cerliponase alfa was initially denied, and after submission of additional analyses/data, Breakthrough Therapy Designation was granted on August 27, 2016.
Brineura received a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher.
There was no Advisory Committee Meeting. All scientific and methodological review issues regarding the Brineura clinical program were clarified and addressed by the different review teams.

requirement.text: 3207-5: Conduct a clinical trial (Study 190-203) to evaluate the short-term safety of Brineura in CLN2 patients below the age of 2 years, assessing serious hypersensitivity reactions and serious device-related complications.

citations.quote: 3207-5 Conduct a clinical trial (Study 190-203) to evaluate the short-term safety of Brineura (cerliponase alfa) in CLN2 patients below the age of 2 years. The trial will assess the risks of serious hypersensitivity reactions, and serious device related complications with short-term use. Perform a root-cause analysis on any device related complications and/or failures including, but not limited to, an analysis of the material integrity of the intraventricular access device reservoir. In addition, this trial will evaluate the effects of serious adverse events on patient performance on the CLN2 motor and language clinical scales.
